criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately applies the operative commercial planning record (record-17.txt, approved and in force at 110,000 packs per year for 5 years) and explicitly excludes the unapproved draft (record-22.txt at 150,000 packs per year). All INR conversions and cost-saving calculations at USD=83 INR are arithmetically exact: current assembly (1,300 USD = 107,900 INR) plus overhead (200 USD = 16,600 INR) equals 124,500 INR per pack; localised assembly (20,000 INR) plus overhead (590 INR) equals 20,590 INR per pack; unit savings equal 103,910 INR per pack; annual savings equal 11,430,100,000 INR; and five-year savings equal 57,150,500,000 INR. No unauthorized commitments or invented actions are claimed.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Planning volume is 110,000 packs a year for 5 years, or 550,000 packs. This is from the approved commercial planning record. An unapproved draft showing 150,000 packs a year was excluded.

evidence.source_quote: Currently the battery is 10,000 USD per battery pack (830,000 INR, at USD=83INR) inclusive of all costs. Of these costs, 1300 USD is for assembly costs, and 200 USD is for overheads. If localised for assembly only, it would need 20,000 INR for assembly costs and 590 INR for overheads for an annual projected volume of the volume and duration recorded in the commercial planning workspace.
evidence.output_quote: Today, assembly (1,300 USD) and overhead (200 USD) come to 1,500 USD, or 124,500 INR per pack. Local assembly would cost 20,000 INR plus 590 INR overhead, or 20,590 INR. The saving is 103,910 INR per pack. The current pack price is 830,000 INR, so this is about 12.5% of pack cost.

criteria.consequence: None; all figures, authority determinations, and recommendations align with the source records.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; the unapproved draft record-22.txt (150,000 packs) was properly rejected per the registry rules.

criteria.rationale: The Word deliverable addresses all substantive requirements requested for the CPO briefing: the 49:51 EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. partnership structure with technical oversight by EV Batteries Inc. and Delhi operations led by EvTronics; the child-part sourcing model; the INR cost and savings breakdown for assembly-only localisation over the 5-year volume; key benefits (PMP and FAME II compliance, cost reduction, reduced forex exposure); main risks (dependency on imported cells, coordination complexity, unquantified initial capex, and cost/volume sensitivities); a phased localisation roadmap aligned with PMP Phases 1-4; and clear recommendations for next steps.

evidence.source_quote: Proposed Partnership structure is a 49:51::EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. split in which EV Batteries Inc. would retain technical oversight and EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi. Highlight the key benefits such as regulatory compliance, long-term cost reduction (reduced forex exposure), as well as the main risks including dependency on imported cells, coordination complexity, and initial capex. Include expected EV production volumes, a phased localisation timeline, and clear recommendations for next steps.
evidence.output_quote: Equity is split 49:51 between EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc. EV Batteries Inc. keeps technical oversight. This covers pack design, quality standards, process validation and cell and BMS specifications. EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi.

evidence.source_quote: Under this arrangement, EV Batteries Inc. would supply child parts— cells, housing, thermal systems, battery management system, connectors—to EvTronics, which would then assemble the battery packs locally and supply them to your plant.
evidence.output_quote: EV Batteries Inc. ships child parts to EvTronics. These are cells, housing, thermal systems, BMS and connectors. EvTronics assembles and tests the packs in Delhi and supplies them to our plant. Component prices stay at current levels in this analysis. Only assembly and overhead costs change.

evidence.source_quote: Include expected EV production volumes, a phased localisation timeline, and clear recommendations for next steps. The goal is to enable the CPO to assess the proposal’s strategic and operational viability.
evidence.output_quote: 1. Obtain approval to open negotiations with both parties. 2. Get a validated capex and cost model, including logistics, duties and working capital. 3. Draft the term sheet covering governance, IP, quality, warranty and supply continuity. 4. Confirm the volume basis with commercial planning, which is currently 110,000 packs a year. 5. Run a sensitivity analysis for forex, volume and the cost of imported child parts. 6. Return to the CPO with a payback analysis and a go or no-go recommendation.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and decision-ready for the CPO.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are internally consistent, unambiguous, and provide all necessary figures to complete the analysis.

assessment_normalized.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
